university: North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University
program_name: MS in Food and Nutritional Sciences
department_or_school: Food and Nutritional Sciences program, Department of Family and Consumer Sciences, College of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences (CAES)
spring_2027_deadline: International spring deadline is September 15 (Graduate College admission page), so the Spring 2027 international deadline (2026-09-15) has PASSED. The department may set earlier deadlines.
fall_2027_deadline: May 15 (international, fall; Graduate College page; presumably 2027-05-15, 2027 dates not posted). January 15 priority FUNDING deadline for fall admission appeared on an older version of the same page.
funding_deadline_note: Apply by about January 15, 2027 for priority funding consideration (fall only; seen on an older version of the Graduate College page, Not verified for 2027).
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate requirement IELTS 6.0 overall (the undergraduate page lists 6.5; the graduate page lists 6.0). Scores valid 2 years.
funding_summary: No program-specific funding statement found for Food and Nutritional Sciences. University assistantship policy: graduate assistants are full-time students employed part-time (up to 20 hrs/week, 0.50 FTE); international students are limited to 50% FTE and 20 hrs/week by immigration law. Tuition waiver and stipend amounts for this program are Not verified.
assistantship_types: GA (university policy: 'graduate assistants', up to 20 hrs/week, 0.50 FTE); program-specific GRA/GTA availability Not verified
assistantship_covers: Not verified (no stipend or tuition-waiver amounts found for this program)
assistantship_deadline: January 15 priority funding deadline (fall), older page version; 2027 Not verified

Students whose immigration status does not allow US employment cannot hold an assistantship. Ask the department directly about current funding. Spring 2027 is closed for international applicants.

program_name: MS in Food, Nutrition, and Culinary Sciences
department_or_school: Department of Food, Nutrition, and Packaging Sciences (FNPS), College of Agriculture, Forestry and Life Sciences
spring_2027_deadline: Rolling admission. FNPS accepts students for Spring, Summer and Fall; the 'final deadline of acceptance is prior to the last day to register for classes' (2025-2026 FNPS graduate handbook). International students should apply much earlier to allow time for a visa; no fixed international date was found.
fall_2027_deadline: Rolling (same rule: final deadline before the last day to register); no fixed Fall 2027 date found
funding_deadline_note: No funding deadline found. GRAs are awarded by individual PIs, so contact prospective advisors early.
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate School: IELTS 'satisfactory score (6.5 or higher)'; valid 2 years. Subscores Not verified.
funding_summary: FNPS graduate handbook (2025-2026): 'The most common mechanism of support is a Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA)'; GRAs are 'awarded on a competitive basis directly by the Principal Investigator of each project'. Teaching assistantships 'are sometimes available but are much less common than GRAs'. Master's (thesis) assistantships 'normally extend for a maximum of two years'. Students are encouraged to contact prospective advisors about GRA availability. FNPS stipend amounts and tuition-waiver terms Not verified.
assistantship_types: GRA (most common, PI-funded); GTA ('sometimes available ... much less common')
assistantship_covers: Not verified for FNPS (stipend amount and tuition-waiver terms not published in the results seen)
notes: International graduate assistants may work up to 20 hrs/week on campus during the semester (Clemson International Services graduate-assistant page). The department was renamed Food, Nutrition, and Packaging Sciences; chair Ramesh Jeganathan (news.clemson.edu) is a former Auburn nutrition professor. Graduate degrees include a Human Nutrition track. Funding depends on finding a PI with a GRA, so advisor contact is effectively required. Graduate faculty advisors verified on FNPS pages (research focus verified only for Haley-Zitlin): Vivian Haley-Zitlin, Professor (type 2 diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome; see w2-r3 professor record); Ramesh Jeganathan, Department Chair and Professor; Elliot Jesch, Associate Professor and Non-thesis Nutrition Advisor (https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/food-nutrition-packaging-sciences/directory/grad-faculty.html; https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/food-nutrition-packaging-sciences/about/contact.html).

program_name: PhD in Health Promotion, Education, and Behavior (Arnold School of Public Health; the school offers no nutrition degree)
department_or_school: Department of Health Promotion, Education, and Behavior, Arnold School of Public Health
funding_deadline_note: Arnold School FAQ: the limited departmental assistantships for international students are awarded 'on a first come, first served basis', so apply early.
funding_summary: Arnold School financial-aid page: graduate assistantships typically require 10-20 hours of work per week and 'may provide a stipend and a special tuition rate' (a reduced rate, not stated as a full waiver). Recipients must be fully admitted, keep a 3.0 GPA and enroll in at least 6 credit hours. Arnold School FAQ: international students (other than permanent residents) are not eligible for traineeships or government loans; 'a limited number of assistantships are available in the departments' at the department's discretion, first come, first served.
assistantship_types: GA ('graduate assistantships ... 10 to 20 hours of work per week')
assistantship_covers: 'may provide a stipend and a special tuition rate' - amounts Not verified; full tuition waiver Not verified
notes: HPEB PhD applicants must contact faculty in their area of interest before applying (program page). The Arnold School FAQ states the school does not offer a nutrition degree. Nutrition-related faculty work through the Arnold School Nutrition Consortium. Related option: MS/PhD in Epidemiology (MS page: https://sc.edu/study/colleges_schools/public_health/degrees-programs/masters/ms-epid.php) for nutrition epidemiology with Angela Liese. International assistantships are 'limited', so this is a weaker funded option than Clemson.

program_name: PhD in Foods and Nutrition / Nutritional Sciences (Graduate School page title: 'PHD, Nutritional Sciences, Community Nutrition Emphasis')
department_or_school: Department of Foods and Nutrition (FDN), College of Family and Consumer Sciences
spring_2027_deadline: International: October 15 (UGA Graduate School general deadline; presumably 2026-10-15, i.e. 4 days from today). FDN page lists Spring 'November 15; funding not typically available' (domestic). Department says funding is limited for spring or summer entry.
fall_2027_deadline: FDN PhD page: Fall July 1, but 'December 10 for full consideration for funding' (presumably 2026-12-10). The Graduate School international fall deadline is April 15. For funding, use Dec 10.
funding_deadline_note: Apply by December 10 (presumably 2026-12-10) for full funding consideration for Fall 2027. Spring entry: 'funding not typically available'.
ielts_subscore_note: Graduate School: overall IELTS band 6.5 with no single band below 6.0; scores no more than 2 years old. The FDN PhD page lists the same minimum. Some UGA departments require higher speaking scores for TAs (e.g., IELTS speaking 8); this is not confirmed for FDN.
funding_summary: No FDN stipend or tuition-waiver amounts found. FDN states department funding is limited for spring or summer entry and gives December 10 as the date for full funding consideration (fall). A UGA search result stated that international students are eligible for assistantships but 'securing a major professor is often a prerequisite' for funding; that FAQ is the Food Science department's, so FDN practice is Not verified.
assistantship_types: Not verified for FDN (UGA uses graduate assistantships, GRA/GTA, requested through the department)
assistantship_deadline: December 10 (full funding consideration, fall); spring funding not typically available
notes: Application: 3 letters, CV, statement of purpose stressing research interests, and unofficial transcripts (UGA Bulletin Nutritional Sciences PhD entry). Sources disagree on dates (Bulletin spring Nov 1 vs FDN Nov 15), so confirm with the graduate coordinator. The department name may be changing to Nutritional Sciences. The community-nutrition emphasis suits her food-insecurity and community interests. Faculty (e.g., Jung Sun Lee) were not verified in this run. If an MS exists, it was not checked.

program_name: MS / PhD in Food Science and Human Nutrition - Nutritional Sciences track (also MS Nutritional Sciences)
department_or_school: Department of Food Science and Human Nutrition (FSHN), UF/IFAS, College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
spring_2027_deadline: No set departmental deadline. FSHN admission page says most students start in Fall but Spring and Summer starts are possible, and recommends that international applicants submit early for admission and visa steps. UF Graduate School international deadline Not verified.
fall_2027_deadline: No set departmental deadline; applications received by January 15 'for the Fall semester start date' are 'competitive for assistantships' (presumably 2027-01-15).
funding_deadline_note: Apply by January 15 (presumably 2027-01-15) to be competitive for assistantships (Fall start).
ielts_subscore_note: UF Graduate Catalog (general Graduate School rule): IELTS 6.5 minimum; the catalog notes a Spring 2027 change to the TOEFL standard (not IELTS). The FSHN admission page on a UF test server lists IELTS 6.0. Either way 6.5 meets it; confirm with FSHN.
funding_summary: FSHN admission page: applications received by January 15 for the Fall start are competitive for assistantships. Admission requires a faculty advisor willing to take the student; applicants with otherwise acceptable credentials are sometimes denied when no faculty member can supervise them. Stipend amount and tuition-waiver terms Not verified.
assistantship_types: Graduate assistantships (type and amount Not verified)
notes: Direct MS admission needs a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 over the last 60 credits (she has 3.85). The GRE is listed among requirements, but whether it still applies for 2027 is Not verified. The admission-page result came from a UF test server (fshn1.test.ifas.ufl.edu), so check the live fshn.ifas.ufl.edu page. The ACEND MS-Dietetic Internship has a separate Jan 15, fall-only deadline. Candidate faculty seen: Wendy Dahl (Professor, dietary fiber, CKD), Zhiyong Cheng (obesity and type 2 diabetes mechanisms), Anne Mathews (associate dean). Amy Mobley (food security and early-childhood obesity) is in the College of Health & Human Performance, not FSHN.

program_name: MS / PhD in Nutrition (Community/Public Health Nutrition and Biomedical Nutrition Science research areas)
department_or_school: Department of Nutrition, College of Education, Health, and Human Sciences (CEHHS)
spring_2027_deadline: PASSED for international applicants: the UT catalog lists international application deadlines of Fall Feb 1, Spring June 15 (2026-06-15 for Spring 2027) and Summer Oct 15; international students 'normally enter the fall semester'.
fall_2027_deadline: Nutrition priority/assistantship deadline January 15 (presumably 2027-01-15); Graduate School international fall deadline February 1 (presumably 2027-02-01; file completion May 15 per a departmental page).
funding_deadline_note: Assistantship consideration requires a COMPLETE application by January 15 (presumably 2027-01-15).
ielts_subscore_note: UT graduate catalog: Graduate School required English score is TOEFL 80 iBT (550 paper) or IELTS 6.5 (stated in the conditional-admission context); 'many departments require a higher average than the minimum'. Nutrition's own minimum Not verified.
funding_summary: Department of Nutrition offers teaching, research and general graduate assistantships ('0.25 or 0.50 time over nine months or twelve months'); assistantship consideration requires a complete application by January 15. Graduate School policy: appointments 'on a one-fourth time basis or higher carry a waiver of maintenance, tuition, and mandatory fees for the appointment period' and include student health insurance; typical appointments are 1/4-1/2 time (10-20 hrs/week) with the stipend paid in 9 or 12 monthly installments (https://gradschool.utk.edu/costs-and-funding/graduate-assistantships/). Assistantships are competitive; stipend amounts vary by unit.
assistantship_types: GTA, GRA and general GA ('teaching, research, and general graduate assistantships'), 0.25 or 0.50 FTE
assistantship_covers: 'waiver of maintenance, tuition, and mandatory fees for the appointment period' + student health insurance for appointments of 1/4 time or more (Graduate School); stipend amount for Nutrition Not verified (FY2027 minimums at https://budget.utk.edu/graduate-stipends/)
notes: Research is split into Biomedical Nutrition Science and Community Nutrition Research. Community group (department research page): Sarah Colby, Katie Kavanagh, Jared McGuirt, Hollie Raynor, Marsha Spence. UT has a university 'Food and Nutrition Security' cluster-hiring initiative (https://research.utk.edu/cluster-hire/food-and-nutrition-security/), an institutional investment signal. A UT trial NCT02684214 (Prevention Plus for childhood obesity in food-secure and food-insecure families, 2016-2021) fits her interests. Another UT department requires international GTAs to pass an oral English test (OPIc); not confirmed for Nutrition. The Dietetics/clinical MS track has its own financial-aid page.
